meta.description: A hybrid baguette using both poolish (commercial yeast) and leaven (sourdough starter) — the poolish gives reliable lift and extensibility, the leaven adds flavor complexity. Baked to a deep golden tone with the toasty aroma of freshly popped corn.

equipment: Hand Peel (narrow board or rigid cardboard)

states.title: Prepare Workspace
states.direction: Gather all vessels, equipment, and ingredients. Weigh out flour, water, salt, yeast, and starter into separate containers. Have rice flour accessible for dusting.
states.exit_condition: All ingredients weighed, vessels and equipment laid out

notes.text: Rice flour is for dusting only — it prevents sticking without absorbing into the dough

states.title: Mix Poolish
states.direction: In large mixing bowl (V1), combine 200g all-purpose flour, 200g water at 75°F (24°C), and 3g active dry yeast. Stir until no dry flour remains.
states.exit_condition: Poolish mixed, no dry flour visible

notes.text: A poolish is a pre-ferment made with equal parts flour and water plus a small amount of commercial yeast. It develops flavor complexity and improves dough extensibility — a classic French baguette technique.

states.title: Ferment Poolish
states.direction: Cover bowl and let poolish stand at warm room temperature 75–80°F (24–27°C) for 3 to 4 hours. Alternatively, ferment overnight in the refrigerator.
states.exit_condition: Poolish is bubbly, domed, and passes the float test — a small spoonful floats in water

notes.text: Overnight refrigerator method: mix poolish before bed, use next morning
If poolish sinks in float test, it needs more time to ferment

states.title: Feed Leaven
states.direction: In medium bowl (V2), place 15g mature starter. Add 220g all-purpose flour and 220g water at 80°F (27°C). Mix thoroughly.
states.exit_condition: Leaven mixed, no dry flour visible

notes.text: Time the leaven so it peaks when the poolish is ready — typically feed leaven 8–12 hours before you plan to mix dough
A leaven (levain) is an active sourdough preferment — a portion of mature starter fed with flour and water and grown to peak activity before mixing into the final dough.

states.title: Ferment Leaven
states.direction: Cover and let leaven ferment at room temperature until it passes the float test. Timing varies by starter strength and ambient temperature, typically 8 to 12 hours.
states.exit_condition: Leaven has risen, is bubbly on surface, and passes the float test

notes.text: Can run in parallel with poolish fermentation — plan timing so both are ready together

states.title: Float Test
states.direction: Drop a small spoonful of poolish into water. Drop a small spoonful of leaven into water. Both must float. If either sinks, it needs more fermentation time.
states.exit_condition: Both poolish and leaven float in water

notes.text: Do not proceed to mixing if either fails the float test — under-fermented pre-ferments will not produce proper bread

states.title: Mix Baguette Dough
states.direction: Pour 500g warm water at 74–76°F (23–24°C) into a large mixing bowl (V1, freed from poolish). Add all the poolish (400g) and 400g of the leaven. Stir to disperse. Add 650g all-purpose flour and 350g bread flour. Mix thoroughly by hand until no dry flour remains. Reserve remaining leaven to refresh your starter.
states.exit_condition: Dough is shaggy but cohesive, no dry flour remains

notes.text: Dough will feel stiffer than basic country dough — it softens during bulk fermentation
Save leftover leaven to refresh and maintain your starter

This recipe uses a hybrid approach: the poolish (yeast-driven) gives reliable lift and extensibility, while the leaven (sourdough-driven) adds flavor complexity and acidity. Together they produce better oven spring than sourdough alone with more depth than straight yeast.

states.title: Autolyse Rest
states.direction: Let the mixed dough rest uncovered for 25 to 40 minutes. Do not add salt yet.
states.exit_condition: Dough has rested 25–40 minutes, feels slightly more extensible

notes.text: Salt is added with the first turn during bulk fermentation, not during mixing

states.title: First Turn — Add Salt
states.direction: Transfer dough to clear container (V3). Sprinkle 24g salt over the dough. Perform a series of stretches and folds: reach under the dough, stretch upward, and fold over itself. Rotate the container and repeat around all sides. Work the salt into the dough.
states.exit_condition: Salt fully incorporated, dough has been stretched and folded from all sides

notes.text: The dough temperature should be about 75°F (24°C) throughout bulk fermentation

states.title: Ferment — Second Turn
states.direction: After 40 minutes, perform another set of stretch-and-folds from all sides of the container.
states.exit_condition: Dough stretched and folded from all sides, container covered

states.title: Ferment — Third Turn
states.direction: After another 40 minutes, perform another set of stretch-and-folds. Dough should be gaining strength and becoming smoother.
states.exit_condition: Dough noticeably stronger and smoother, stretched and folded from all sides

states.title: Ferment — Fourth Turn
states.direction: After another 40 minutes, perform the final set of stretch-and-folds. Handle the dough gently — it should be airy and billowy.
states.exit_condition: Dough is airy, billowy, and shows good fermentation activity

notes.text: Be gentle — the dough has developed significant gas by now

states.title: Complete Bulk Fermentation
states.direction: Let dough continue to ferment undisturbed for the remaining time. Total bulk fermentation is 3 to 4 hours from the first turn.
states.exit_condition: Dough has increased 20–30% in volume, feels airy and jiggly, surface shows bubbles

notes.text: Look for the dough to feel alive — it should jiggle when you move the container

states.title: Divide Dough
states.direction: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Using a bench scraper, divide into 2 or 3 equal pieces depending on the size of your baking stone.
states.exit_condition: Dough divided into 2 or 3 equal pieces

notes.text: For a standard home baking stone, 3 shorter baguettes are easier to manage than 2 long ones

states.title: Pre-shape
states.direction: Shape each piece into a rectangle with rounded corners. Use gentle hands — preserve as much gas as possible.
states.exit_condition: Each piece shaped into a loose rectangle with rounded corners

states.title: Bench Rest
states.direction: Let the pre-shaped pieces rest on the work surface, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough has relaxed and spread slightly, 30 minutes elapsed

notes.text: Use this time to prepare the couche

states.title: Prepare Couche
states.direction: Drape a large kitchen towel over a baking sheet or cutting board (V4). Dust generously with rice flour.
states.exit_condition: Couche prepared with generous rice flour dusting

notes.text: A couche (French for 'bed') is a stiff cloth used to support baguettes during final proof — the folds between loaves prevent sideways spreading. Bread baskets (bannetons) are for round/oval loaves; baguettes need the couche's elongated support.

states.title: Shape Baguettes
states.direction: Working with one piece at a time: fold the third closest to you up and over the middle third. Hold the ends and stretch horizontally to double the width. Fold the far third over the middle like closing an envelope flap. Press the flap to build tension. Using palms and fingers, roll the dough toward you, pressing with the outer edge of palms to develop tension with each roll. Place both palms on the cylinder and roll back and forth, stretching to elongate and taper the ends. Keep the length appropriate for your baking stone.
states.exit_condition: Baguettes shaped into tapered cylinders with good surface tension, sized to fit baking stone

notes.text: The shape should resemble a French rolling pin — tapered at the ends, even in the middle
Keep the seam tight — loose seams cause the loaf to open during baking

states.title: Place on Couche
states.direction: Place shaped baguettes seam-side up on the floured towel. Separate them with folds in the towel. Bring the sides of the towel over the outer loaves to support the edges.
states.exit_condition: All baguettes on couche, separated by towel folds, outer edges supported

states.title: Proof Baguettes
states.direction: Let baguettes rise at warm room temperature 70–75°F (21–24°C) for 2.5 to 3 hours.
states.exit_condition: Baguettes have visibly expanded, dough springs back slowly when gently poked

notes.text: Begin preheating oven with steam setup at least 45 minutes before proof is complete

states.title: Set Up Steam
states.direction: Soak 2–3 kitchen towels in water. Line a rimmed baking sheet (V6) with the soaked towels. Place on the bottom rack of the oven.
states.exit_condition: Rimmed baking sheet with soaked towels placed on bottom oven rack

notes.text: The wet towels create sustained steam — they should be thoroughly saturated

states.title: Preheat Oven
states.direction: Place baking stone (V5) on the middle rack. Preheat oven to 500°F (260°C) with the steam pan already inside. The oven should steam for at least 15 minutes before loading.
states.exit_condition: Oven at 500°F (260°C), baking stone fully heated, oven visibly steaming

notes.text: A fully preheated stone is essential for oven spring — do not rush this step

states.title: Score and Load Baguettes
states.direction: Dust pizza peel with rice flour. Dust the seam side of the baguettes with rice flour. Flip each loaf onto the hand peel using the couche towel, then slide onto the pizza peel. Arrange baguettes about 5cm apart. Score each loaf down the center with a series of slightly overlapping lines using the razor blade lame. Open oven door, slide baguettes onto the baking stone, and quickly shut the door. Immediately reduce oven temperature to 475°F (246°C).
states.exit_condition: Baguettes scored and loaded onto baking stone, oven door shut, temperature reduced to 475°F (246°C)

notes.text: Work quickly — every second the oven door is open, you lose steam and heat
Score with confident, swift strokes — hesitation tears the dough

states.title: Bake with Steam
states.direction: Bake baguettes with the steam pan in place. The steam helps develop the crust. Watch for the baguettes to start taking on color.
states.exit_condition: Baguettes are beginning to color, approximately 15 minutes elapsed

notes.text: Do not open the oven during this phase — steam retention is critical for crust development

states.title: Bake without Steam
states.direction: Carefully remove the steam pan with the dried kitchen towels. Continue baking until baguettes reach a deep golden color.
states.exit_condition: Baguettes are deep golden brown, loaves sound hollow when tapped on the bottom

notes.text: Use oven mitts — the steam pan and towels are extremely hot
Push for deep golden, not pale — the dark crust is where the toasty corn aroma lives

states.title: Cool
states.direction: Transfer baguettes to a wire rack. Serve warm from the oven or let cool completely.
states.exit_condition: Baguettes on cooling rack, crust is crackling as it cools

notes.text: The crust will soften if cooled on a flat surface — always use a rack for air circulation
Listen for the crust to crackle and sing as it cools — a sign of a well-baked loaf

methods.detail: 350°F (175°C), 5–10 min. Spritz crust with water before reheating for crispness.
Paper bag at room temp, same day. Freeze sliced in zip-lock for longer storage.
